Sampling methods a study can declare

Source: R/study.R
sframe_sampling_methods.Rd

The fixed list study$sampling$method is checked against.

  • Probability methods: "simple_random", "systematic", "stratified" and "cluster". Every member of the population has a known chance of selection.

  • Non-probability methods: "convenience", "purposive", "quota" and "snowball". A report says the sample is a non-probability one, so its results do not generalise to the population by sampling theory.

  • "census": the whole population is asked.

  • "other": described in study$sampling$method_other, which is then required.

Usage

sframe_sampling_methods(
  type = c("all", "probability", "non_probability", "census")
)

Arguments

type

"all" (the default), "probability", "non_probability" or "census".

Value

A character vector.

See also

Other Design functions: as_sframe(), launch_builder(), read_sframe(), sframe_attention_check(), sframe_branch(), sframe_choice_set(), sframe_conjoint_design(), sframe_get_study(), sframe_instrument(), sframe_item(), sframe_scale(), sframe_validation, validate_sframe(), write_sframe()

Examples

sframe_sampling_methods()
#>  [1] "simple_random" "systematic"    "stratified"    "cluster"      
#>  [5] "convenience"   "purposive"     "quota"         "snowball"     
#>  [9] "census"        "other"        
sframe_sampling_methods("non_probability")
#> [1] "convenience" "purposive"   "quota"       "snowball"
